result.text: Title: Storage management First, the order is read from the automatic order management system.
Then, it's checked if the first product from the order is in stock.
If it's in stock then it's withdrawn from the warehouse.
However, if it's not in stock then it's reordered from the wholesaler.
Note, that if it was necessary to wait more then 10 days for the arrival of the product then a delivery delay penalty is automatically demanded from the wholesaler.
After the ordered product has arrived it's registered in the stock management system.
Finally, it's checked if the whole order is ready for shipment.
If the order is ready for shipment, a courier is requested and the products are packed simultaneously and finally shipped.
If it isn't then the next product from the order is selected and the process starts again with checking if this order is in stock or not.

Title: Storage management

First, the order is read from the automatic order management system.
Then, it's checked if the first product from the order is in stock.
If it's in stock then it's withdrawn from the warehouse.
However, if it's not in stock then it's reordered from the wholesaler.
Note, that if it was necessary to wait more then 10 days for the arrival of the  product then a delivery delay penalty is automatically demanded from the wholesaler.
After the ordered product has arrived it's registered in the stock management system.
Finally, it's checked if the whole order is ready for shipment.
If the order is ready for shipment, a courier is requested and the products are packed simultaneously and finally shipped.
If it isn't then the next product from the order is selected and the process starts again with checking if this order is in stock or not.

result.rule: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

result.rule: When the description says that after a prior step, the process must wait for an external party to respond or arrive at a time not fixed in advance, and a later step or decision depends on that response or arrival: Model an intermediate catch event that represents the wait between the prior step and the dependent step or gateway. Do not fold the waiting into the prior task, do not model the wait as a separate task, and do not connect the two steps with a plain sequence flow that hides the wait.

When the description says the process waits until an external milestone is reached (for example, an item arriving at a recipient's location) and later steps depend on that milestone having occurred: Model the wait as an intermediate catch event, not a task, and name that catch event with the milestone as the description states it, so the stage stays identifiable in the model. Do not replace the wait with a task, and do not leave the milestone unnamed or rename it to a generic label.

When the description says the process waits for a response from an outside party or group, or until a period of time or a later point in time has passed, whichever comes first, before it continues to a decision or the next step: Model the wait as an event-based gateway. Give one branch an intermediate message catch event for the expected response. Give the other branch an intermediate timer catch event for the stated duration or point in time. Place any step the description ties to the timeout (for example, escalating or forwarding) after the timer event. Do not model the wait as an extra task or as sequential catch events, because the description states a race between the two outcomes.

When the description says that an activity follows the receipt of an item or delivery (for example 'upon receiving X, ...'), and it does not describe any message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for: Do not insert an intermediate catch event for the receipt. Connect the preceding activity directly by a sequence flow to the first activity the description gives after the receipt. Use an intermediate catch event only when the description states a wait for an external message, signal, timer or condition.

Do not substitute an evaluative verb, a paraphrase, or a follow-up action that the description does not state. When the arrival is an external occurrence the process waits for, model it as an intermediate catch event labeled with the item name, not as a task.

When the description sends a request or demand to an outside party and then states a deadline or time limit for the reply, and the flow continues on whichever comes first: the reply or the expiry of that time limit: Model the wait after the request as an event-based gateway. One branch is the event that the reply arrives. The other branch is an intermediate timer catch event for the stated time limit. Connect the timer branch to the path the description takes when the deadline passes. Do not model the deadline wait as an ordinary task.

When the description says that an activity follows the receipt of an item or delivery (for example 'upon receiving X, ...'), and it does not describe any message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for: Do not insert an intermediate catch event for the receipt. result.rule: When the description says the process starts when a party (such as a department) performs a stated action, for example identifying a need, before any further work is described: Model a start event for the triggering occurrence, and place a separate task directly after it that is named with the action the party performs. Do not fold that action into the start event's label. Connect the task to the next step of the described flow.

When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action (for example, filling in information or signing up) that is followed by further system activity: Model the process start as a plain start event, then model the participant's described action as a task placed after it and before the next system activity. Do not use the action as the label of the start event.

When the description says the process begins when a participant performs a named action, and that same action is also described as a step the participant carries out: Model a start event that marks the beginning of the process, followed by a task that carries the named action as an activity. Do not use the start event's label as the only representation of that action, so the action appears as a task in the flow.

When the description says the process starts when a party performs a stated action (for example, submitting something) and names no message, signal, or other message exchange that the action sends: Model the process start as a bpmn:startEvent with no incoming sequence flow. Place a plain bpmn:task (not a bpmn:sendTask) for the party's action directly after the start event, and connect it by a sequence flow to the next step of the described flow. Do not add a second start event for the action, and do not add an end event after the action.
